questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Transhistorical
questions.solution: Transhistorical means transcending history; eternal or timeless.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Glib
questions.solution: Glib means fluent and voluble but often insincere and shallow. Articulate is the closest synonym regarding fluency.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Cogent
questions.solution: Cogent means (of an argument or case) clear, logical, and convincing.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Historiographical
questions.solution: Historiographical relates to the study of the writing of history and historical theories.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Bellicose
questions.solution: Bellicose means demonstrating aggression and willingness to fight.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Integrity
questions.solution: Integrity is the quality of being honest and having strong moral principles.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Quixotic
questions.solution: Quixotic means exceedingly idealistic; unrealistic and impractical.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Dread
questions.solution: Dread means to anticipate with great apprehension or fear.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Mythopoeic
questions.solution: Mythopoeic relates to the making of myths or causing myths to be made.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Pernicious
questions.solution: Pernicious means having a harmful effect, especially in a gradual or subtle way. Malicious means intending to do harm.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Existential
questions.solution: Existential relates to existence, often associated with the philosophical theory of existentialism emphasizing individual existence, freedom and choice.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Renounce
questions.solution: Renounce means to formally declare one's abandonment of (a claim, right, or possession).

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Wisdom
questions.solution: Wisdom involves having experience, knowledge, and good judgment.

questions.question: Choose the correct word from the options given showing a synonym of the word below: Garrulous
questions.solution: Garrulous means excessively talkative. Loquacious is a direct synonym.

questions.question: Choose the option which is similar in meaning to the underlined word: Columbus was convinced that the earth was round.
questions.solution: Convinced means completely certain about something. Assured means confident.

questions.question: Choose the option which is similar in meaning to the underlined word: It’s incredible to see him in such good health after the accident.
questions.solution: Incredible means impossible to believe. Unimaginable means difficult or impossible to imagine or comprehend.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Sagacious
questions.solution: Sagacious means having or showing keen mental discernment and good judgment.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Clout
questions.solution: Clout refers to influence or power, especially in politics or business.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate synonym of the word: Mirage
questions.solution: A Mirage is an optical illusion or something illusory. Fantasy represents something imaginary.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Credulous
questions.solution: Credulous means showing too great a readiness to believe things. Skeptical means not easily convinced; having doubts.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Ineffable
questions.solution: Ineffable means too great or extreme to be expressed or described in words.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Ignorance
questions.solution: Ignorance is lack of knowledge or information.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Iconoclast
questions.solution: An Iconoclast attacks cherished beliefs or institutions. A Conformist conforms to accepted behavior or established practices.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Profuse
questions.solution: Profuse means exuberant; plentiful; abundant. Scarce means insufficient for the demand.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Fastidious
questions.solution: Fastidious means very attentive to and concerned about accuracy and detail. Sloppy means careless and unsystematic.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Immutable
questions.solution: Immutable means unchanging over time or unable to be changed. Alterable means capable of being changed.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Debacle
questions.solution: A Debacle is a sudden and ignominious failure; a fiasco.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Minute
questions.solution: Minute (pronounced my-noot) means extremely small. Enormous means very large.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Extinguished
questions.solution: Extinguish means to cause a fire to cease to burn. Ignite means to catch fire or cause to catch fire.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Trivial
questions.solution: Trivial means of little value or importance.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Ebullient
questions.solution: Ebullient means cheerful and full of energy. Depressed means in a state of general unhappiness.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Heresy
questions.solution: Heresy is belief or opinion contrary to orthodox religious (especially Christian) doctrine. Orthodoxy is authorized or generally accepted theory, doctrine, or practice.

questions.question: What is the antonym of "Disparate"?
questions.solution: Disparate means essentially different in kind; not allowing comparison. Similar means resembling without being identical.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Hegemony
questions.solution: Hegemony is leadership or dominance, especially by one country or social group. Subordination is the state of being lower in rank or position.

questions.question: Select the antonym of Contumacious”?
questions.solution: Contumacious means stubbornly or willfully disobedient to authority.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Foment
questions.solution: Foment means to instigate or stir up (an undesirable or violent sentiment or course of action). Quash means to suppress or put an end to.

questions.question: What is the antonym of "Evanescent"?
questions.solution: Evanescent means soon passing out of sight, memory, or existence; quickly fading. Enduring means lasting over a period of time.

questions.question: What is the antonym of ‘Ephemeral’?
questions.solution: Ephemeral means lasting for a very short time. Eternal means lasting or existing forever.

questions.question: What is the antonym of Tenebrous”?
questions.solution: Tenebrous means dark; shadowy or obscure.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Exacerbate
questions.solution: Exacerbate means to make (a problem, bad situation, or negative feeling) worse. Improve means to make or become better.

questions.question: What is the antonym of misanthropic”?
questions.solution: Misanthropic means disliking humankind and avoiding human society. Sociable means willing to talk and engage in activities with other people.

questions.question: What is the antonym of ‘Quaint’?
questions.solution: Quaint means attractively unusual or old-fashioned. Ordinary means having no special or distinctive features; normal.

questions.question: What is the antonym of obloquy”?
questions.solution: Obloquy means strong public criticism or verbal abuse.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Garrulous
questions.solution: Garrulous means excessively talkative. Reserved implies being slow to reveal emotion or opinions.

questions.question: What is the antonym of ineluctable”?
questions.solution: Ineluctable means unable to be resisted or avoided; inescapable. Preventable means able to be avoided.

questions.question: What is the antonym of ‘Turbulent’?
questions.solution: Turbulent means characterized by conflict, disorder, or confusion.

questions.question: What is the antonym of Egalitarian”?
questions.solution: Egalitarian refers to the principle that all people are equal. Biased implies unfair prejudice for or against someone or something.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Monstrous
questions.solution: Monstrous can mean ugly or frightening. Beautiful is the opposite in terms of aesthetics.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Elucidate
questions.solution: Elucidate means to make (something) clear; explain. Obscure means to keep from being seen; conceal.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Euphemism
questions.solution: A Euphemism is a mild or indirect word or expression substituted for one considered to be too harsh or blunt. Directness is the quality of being plain and straightforward.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Obsolete
questions.solution: Obsolete means no longer produced or used; out of date. Current means belonging to the present time.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Cajole
questions.solution: Cajole means to persuade someone to do something by sustained coaxing or flattery. Bully implies using force or threats.

questions.question: Select the most appropriate antonym of the word: Sporadic
questions.solution: Sporadic means occurring at irregular intervals or only in a few places. Frequent means occurring or done on many occasions.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences uses the word "minute" with the same meaning as in the following sentence: "The microscope revealed a minute speck of dust"
options: The meeting will start in a few minutes.
I was just a minute away from being late.
The camera captured every minute detail of the insect's wing.
The alarm went off in exactly sixty seconds, or one minute.
questions.solution: In the question, minute (pronounced my-noot) is an adjective meaning extremely small. Option 3 uses it in the same sense ("minute detail").

questions.question: Which of the following sentences uses the word "tire" with the same meaning as in the following sentence: "I am starting to tire of this long journey"
options: My bicycle has a flat tire.
The mechanic replaced the old tire.
The baby started to tire of playing with the same toy.
We needed to put air in the car’s tire.
questions.solution: Here, tire is a verb meaning to lose interest or become weary. Option 3 uses it in the same sense.

questions.question: Which of the following sentences uses the word "tear" with the same meaning as in the following sentence: "A single tear rolled down her cheek"
options: He carefully tried not to tear the delicate fabric.
The little girl's tear brought her mother running.
Be careful not to tear the pages of the old book.
The sharp edge of the paper can easily tear when handled roughly.
questions.solution: Here, tear (rhymes with ear) is a noun meaning a drop of salty liquid from the eye. Option 2 matches this meaning.
